summary: The Linux provider of the application-scoped Runic.Platform services: XDG desktop portals, D-Bus services and freedesktop.org specifications, with one application identity and diagnostic sink for all of them.

p: Configure once at application composition. Each service retains its own connection and lifetime; this object requires no disposal. A supplied host ID requires a matching installed desktop entry. Omitting the ID retains desktop-inferred identity for development or externally identified applications.
Windows and macOS have static providers (

) because their identity comes from the process: the AppUserModelID or the bundle. On Linux the portals identify the application by the desktop ID it registers once per connection, and report setup problems to the sink, so both live on this object.
Window services (file dialogs, the clipboard and file handoff) belong to a window: Runic's hosts create them for each window, such as

summary: The installed reverse-DNS application identifier, or null for desktop-inferred identity.
Creates the desktop's application database: content types, installed applications, default applications and icons, read from the freedesktop.org files.
remarks: It needs no window and reads the XDG directories from the environment of this process when created. Only the icon theme lookup and D-Bus-activatable launches use the session bus. Inside Flatpak or Snap the host's applications are out of reach; content types and icons come from the sandbox's own data.

summary: Creates application-scoped idle power inhibition, as the Windows and macOS providers do.
remarks: Each request sends the empty parent window identifier, which the Inhibit portal accepts, so the request belongs to the application rather than to a window and works without one.

summary: Creates the user's trash, following the freedesktop.org Trash specification.
remarks: It needs no window. Outside a sandbox it moves items into
, or into the trash at the top of the item's mount; inside Flatpak or Snap it asks the Trash portal.

summary: Creates explicitly unparented file dialogs for an application without a window.
remarks: Linux only: the portal may show such a dialog without a parent. Windows in a Runic host get dialogs owned by the window from the host instead.

summary: Creates the desktop's storage volumes from UDisks2 on the system bus.
remarks: UDisks2 asks Polkit for authorization itself and may show a prompt. The volumes need no portal and no window; a sandbox must allow talking to
on the system bus. Creating them connects to nothing; the first request does.
